text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The attorney-general publishes bills seeking to dismantle the Kenya Posts and Telecommunications Corporation and replace it with four independent institutions.
- An authority to license and regulate the operations of all pension fund schemes, including the National Social Security Fund, will be established if parliament passes a new bill.
- Police recover another 3.3 million shillings believed to part of the 96 million stolen from the Standard Chartered Bank in February.
- A Nairobi principal magistrate is charged with corruptly soliciting one million shillings from a couple charged with criminal offences.
- Thousands of insurance agents fear losing their jobs if the government's recent directive to professionalise agencies by the end of the year is implemented.
- Mwai Kibaki, chairman of opposition Democratic Party moves to lock out anyone other than himself from being nominated as the party's presidential candidate.
- President Daniel arap Moi postpones the reopening of parliament to April this year instead of March 25.
- A full scale corporate war breaks out betwen the executive chairman of the giant Kenya Commercial Bank Alexander Kaminchia and his general manager Elijah arap Bii.

- A summons from the Public Accounts Committee to business tycoon Ketan Somaia over the uncompleted delivery of security equipment puts opposition leader and chairman of the PAC in deeper political problems. ($1=55 Kenyan shillings)
